title: Coalfire pentesters arrested at Dallas County Courthouse
summary: Two Coalfire operators were arrested during an authorized physical penetration test of the Dallas County, Iowa courthouse; charges were later dropped and the county reached a settlement. A canonical lessons-learned case on scope, authorization, and law-enforcement contact.

title: Iowa Judicial Branch investigation report on the Coalfire engagement
summary: The State Court Administration's official investigation into the Coalfire courthouse arrests. Finds that unclear scope on after-hours testing and the absence of any legal review of the engagement documents drove the confrontation. The primary authorization-and-scope reference for this case.

title: Users Really Do Plug in USB Drives They Find
summary: Field study that dropped 297 USB drives on a university campus and measured how many were plugged in; a large share were. Empirical basis for USB drop tradecraft.

title: Stuxnet and the air-gap USB vector
summary: Malware widely reported to have reached air-gapped industrial systems via removable media. Illustrates a physical introduction vector into an isolated network; specific attribution is widely reported rather than adjudicated.

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1200: Hardware Additions
summary: ATT&CK reference page for introducing computer accessories, networking hardware, or devices into a system or network as an initial-access vector.

title: MITRE ATT&CK T1091: Replication Through Removable Media
summary: ATT&CK reference page for moving onto systems, including air-gapped networks, by copying malware to removable media.

title: Huawei drone surveillance in the TDC 5G contract fight
summary: During the fight over TDC's ~EUR 200M 5G contract, a large drone was reportedly seen scanning an investigation room whiteboard in Copenhagen and later monitoring TDC's executive team before descending into a waiting van. Reported by Bloomberg as part of an alleged Huawei espionage effort; Huawei denies involvement, so attribution is reported rather than adjudicated.

title: Pine Risk Management: Lessons Learned
summary: A curated collection of physical red-team lessons learned and near-misses from internal assessments and peer-shared incidents, aimed at improving tradecraft and safety on engagements.

title: Antwerp diamond heist (School of Turin)
summary: Thieves defeated multiple layers of vault security at the Antwerp Diamond Center and emptied scores of safe deposit boxes in one of the largest diamond heists on record. Wired's long-form account details the reconnaissance and bypass tradecraft involved.

title: Cargo thieves steal $1.3M in copper wire and data center gear
summary: Two trailers of data center materials, including about $300,000 in copper wire, were stolen in the Southeast and recovered at a truck yard near Chicago via GPS tracking. Part of a sharp 2025 rise in organized cargo theft targeting AI data center supply chains.

title: Louvre crown jewels heist and its security failures
summary: Thieves posing as workers used a truck mounted furniture lift to reach a first floor gallery, cut into display cases, and left with French crown jewels in minutes. Later reporting flagged monitoring gaps, including exterior cameras that did not cover the balcony used for entry.

title: Deviant Ollam: I'll Let Myself In (Tactics of Physical Pen Testers)
summary: Widely cited overview of physical penetration testing tradecraft: bypassing doors and locks, exploiting request to exit sensors, and using pretext to move through buildings.

title: Elevator Hacking: From the Pit to the Penthouse (Ollam & Payne)
summary: DEF CON 22 talk on how elevators undermine building access control, covering recall keys, hoistway access, and reaching floors that badge systems are meant to restrict.

title: Jayson Street: Steal Everything, Kill Everyone, Cause Total Financial Ruin!
summary: DEF CON 19 talk walking through real social engineering and physical intrusion engagements against banks and enterprises, showing how easily an on site attacker can walk in and misbehave.

title: Jayson Street: Breaking in Bad (I'm the One Who Doesn't Knock)
summary: Social Engineering Village talk sharing attack vectors and stories from physical engagements, focused on how attackers gain trust and physical access on site.

title: Silent Ransom Group hires burglars to breach US law firms
technique: Insider recruitment; Impersonation/Pretext; Media drop (USB); Surveillance/Recon
summary: The FBI and investigators allege the Russian-speaking Silent Ransom Group hired people in the US to enter major law firms in person, posing as IT support, plug in USB drives, and use smart glasses to stream the office, to steal client data for ransom. Attribution is alleged; a later US indictment is the secondary source.

title: GAO covert testing: investigators smuggle bomb components into federal buildings
summary: US Government Accountability Office investigators used covert testing to carry bomb making components past security at 10 of 10 high security federal buildings, then assembled a device inside and moved through offices. A benchmark result for authorized physical red teaming at scale.

title: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum heist
summary: Two men posing as police officers talked their way into the museum after hours, restrained the guards, and left with 13 works valued over $500 million. The largest property crime in US history, still unsolved, and a classic case of authority based pretext.

title: Hatton Garden safe deposit burglary
summary: Over a holiday weekend, a crew disabled the lift, climbed down the shaft, and drilled through a thick vault wall to empty safe deposit boxes in London's jewelry district. A textbook covert entry that exploited timing and gaps in physical monitoring.

title: Francis Brown: RFID Hacking (Live Free or RFID Hard)
summary: DEF CON 21 talk on long range RFID badge theft and cloning, introducing the Tastic RFID Thief that silently reads proximity cards from a few feet away to clone employee badges and reach restricted areas.

title: RTV Overflow: Physical Red Teaming for Offensive Cyber Teams
summary: Talk on bringing physical red teaming into offensive cyber work: how in person access complements network operations, common entry and pretext techniques, and how to scope and run physical engagements. Presented by Ana Aslanishvili and Shawn Abelson.

title: DEF CON 33: From Pwn to Plan (Turning Physical Exploits Into Upgrades)
summary: DEF CON 33 talk on translating physical penetration test findings into concrete security upgrades, framing physical exploits as inputs to a remediation plan rather than one off wins.

title: Y-12 nuclear complex break-in by peace activists
summary: Three peace activists, one an 82 year old nun, cut through four fences and walked nearly a mile to reach the highly enriched uranium storage building at the Y-12 complex, going undetected for hours. Called the biggest security breach in the history of the US atomic complex.

title: Barclays branch KVM heist by a fake IT engineer
summary: A man posing as an IT engineer walked into a London Barclays branch, said he was there to fix a computer, and plugged a keyboard video mouse device into a PC that let the crew control it remotely and move about 1.3 million pounds. A near identical attempt hit Santander.

title: Brussels Airport diamond heist
summary: Eight men in police style uniforms and cars cut a hole in the airport perimeter fence, drove onto the tarmac, and took about 50 million dollars in diamonds from the hold of a parked plane in roughly five minutes, without firing a shot.

title: Las Vegas Strip hotel room heists using under door tools
summary: Investigative reporting on thieves entering occupied hotel rooms on the Las Vegas Strip while guests sleep, in some cases using an under door tool that reaches beneath the door to release the interior handle and bypass the deadbolt. Reported losses include tens of thousands in cash, watches, and jewelry.

title: Onity hotel keycard lock hack used in real burglaries
summary: Researcher Cody Brocious showed a roughly 50 dollar Arduino gadget that plugs into the port beneath an Onity hotel lock and opens it in seconds by defeating weak crypto. The flaw affected millions of locks and was then used in real hotel burglaries, including a string of break ins in Texas.

title: Casino breached through a lobby fish tank thermometer
summary: Attackers used an internet connected thermometer in a casino lobby aquarium as a foothold on the network, then located the high roller database and pulled it back out through the same device. Recounted by Darktrace as a case of an on premises IoT device opening the way in; the casino is unnamed.
